# Today on Hacker News

---

## 🤖 AI / ML

The AI conversation is buzzing today with a mix of excitement and skepticism. **"Notes from the Mistral AI Now Summit"** offers a firsthand look at the latest from one of Europe's leading AI labs, while **"Liquid AI reveals 8B-A1B MoE trained on 38T"** highlights the relentless pace of model development — a compact Mixture-of-Experts model trained on a staggering 38 trillion tokens. On the more critical side, **"Is AI causing a repeat of frontend's lost decade?"** sparks debate about whether AI tooling is leading developers toward the same productivity traps that plagued frontend engineering for years. Meanwhile, **"MCP Is Dead"** questions the longevity of the Model Context Protocol, and **"Shift will clean homes for free to train future robots"** raises eyebrows about the real-world data collection strategies companies are deploying to train physical AI systems. Finally, **"Tiny-vLLM – high performance LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA"** is a Show HN gem for anyone looking to run LLM inference efficiently at the metal level.

---

## 💻 Programming & Engineering

Developers had plenty to chew on today. **"SQLite is all you need for durable workflows"** makes a compelling case for leaning on SQLite as the backbone of reliable, stateful systems — a refreshingly simple take in a world of overengineered stacks. **"Bijou64: A variable-length integer encoding"** from Ink & Switch dives into the elegant design of a new compact integer format. **"On Rendering Diffs"** is a thoughtful exploration of the surprisingly complex problem of displaying code changes in a human-friendly way. And **"You can just say it"** — from Redis creator antirez — encourages developers to communicate more directly and honestly in technical writing and code reviews.

---

## 🖥️ Hardware & Gadgets

Hardware enthusiasts had two standout stories. **"It's hard to justify buying a Framework 12"** is a candid review from Jeff Geerling, who finds the modular laptop's value proposition underwhelming at its current price point — a must-read for anyone eyeing the latest Framework release. On the maker/3D printing side, **"Print with dozens of colors: Our new open-source ColorMix for PrusaSlicer"** from Prusa introduces a new open-source color mixing feature that could meaningfully expand what desktop 3D printers can produce.

---

## 🌍 Economics & Society

The most-discussed post of the day ventures well outside tech: **"The dead economy theory"** (613 points, 800+ comments) presents a provocative macroeconomic argument that deserves attention. **"The California state assembly has passed the 'Protect Our Games Act'"** is a win for the Stop Killing Games movement, requiring publishers to keep games playable even after official support ends — a landmark moment for digital consumer rights. Rounding things out, **"Free full BGP feed. IPv4 and IPv6"** is a niche but appreciated resource for network engineers needing access to full routing table data.

---
